### 2026-10-31: # October 31st (1): Getting on Track

**1h**

# October 31st (1): Getting on Track

I am brand new to everything in hardware, Half Life is the first time I've ever done these kinds of things. Because of this, the new starter project guide style confused me, and left me very lost without a structured tutorial to follow. I knew what I wanted to make, just no idea how to start. I added 2 parts in my schematic, ones I remember from previous projects and just stared at them, no idea what do next.

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 2.52.49 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/25b7d795f89ff131f844af197a25d0bbe1fbf66e13f5173cc3aca16bcd92b7ac.png)

Which pin is VCC and which one is GND?  Do I have to add in the glass panel by myself? If I don't, will I not have one? Do I need a glass panel? What's a LiPo? What parts do I need?

Thus, I spent one hour with my father looking through the OLED screen guide and just... orienting myself.

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 3.01.01 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/4abddaa2ec6265820c60753dfd034ead55f0cb733e714629dd7cc08fab643b15.png)

I have to check the listing for the order of the pins to know which is which, and wire them in order. Yes, I need a glass panel, and I can buy them preassembled if adding them in is too complicated. A LiPo is a battery, a rechargeable power source. I need the microcontroller and OLED screen, and also decided on adding 4 buttons to cycle between focus and breaks and reset the timer.

Many such questions were answered. A plan was formed. I was no longer wandering around aimlessly, I had a direction labelled on a roadmap to success.

I don't know for sure if these count toward approved hours... but it was a lot of work. Journalling them anyways. Thanks.

Tl;dr: I know what to do now. Finishing the schematic next time.

### 2026-10-31: # October 31st (2): Drawing the Schematic

**1.5h**

# October 31st (2): Drawing the Schematic

3rd time in my entire life using KiCad schematic editor. I feel quite comfortable now!

The only issues I ran into were some confusion on how draw  the capacitors and resistors.

At first, I thought the guide was saying to add symbols called 100 nF, 10 µF, and 4.7 kΩ pull-up, then I realized after googling how to add them in that I have to add symbols called C and R and change the text value. Once I realized how to properly add them, I then tried connected the capacitors to the OLED. Because of the wording in the guide, and my inexperience, it came out in an... interesting way:

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 5.12.26 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/7e9e7b135338a185757c61dc25a5c7b55e83261347eea9795d82d7d98d980510.png)
Something about this looked wrong, so I ran it through Gemini to see if I did it right. Lo and behold, it wasn't, but it explained how to properly connect them and I understood and wired the resistors the same way.

Also, since I added buttons as part of my own design, I was not sure at all how to wire them, but I used the ones I wired on my week 1 project, [Starbie](https://github.com/mithrasagar123-coder/starbie/blob/main/README.md), as reference.

And voila, I was done! Spent a couple extra minutes to organize it all together too.

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 5.06.06 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/5678afa7f11f2c36a1dfd459b2922b79818ef2ab55371afa591a933a2cee5518.png)

Moving on to PCB routing next.

Tl;dr: Finished drawing the schematic. It's all good.

### 2026-11-01: # November 1st (1): Rearranging & Routing

**3.25h**

# November 1st (1): Rearranging & Routing

## Layout

First off, I looked at my design again and made a few changes:
1. I added the PCB edge, which I forgot to do last night. I gave it a nice rounded rectangle shape.
2. I moved the resistors and capacitors to the middle, so it's as close as possible to the microcontroller and OLED screen.
3. I swapped the positions of the microcontroller and OLED because I realized the USB port was trapped in the middle.
4. Moved the mounting holes so they're flush against the edges to keep things compact.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 11.05.23 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/f8aee9fe294c2c8c66362b53ebdbada816eeaa2473bf7e78121f52ae9bbc0994.png)

But even after this, I still wasn't happy. There was still a lot of extra space between the microcontroller and the OLED screen. I wanted to reduce that space as much as possible, because big PCBs are expensive (and I've been going over my tier funding for every single week).

So I thought, what if I move 2 switches to the other edge of the board? But this would make wiring more difficult, so  I went back to my schematic to move things around. While I was doing this, I realized I never put in the blue X's on unused pins, which I'm really glad I caught now.

 Updated schematic:
![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 11.22.23 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/08afa696c6995f0810ae1bb016abf7f7a26c1706135244aade839ba40f1ecd8c.png)

Went back to PCB editor, and switched everything up.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 11.43.10 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/78171039b6538f5fd67604fba39d6c4814048b16a04f69846d715d3113d83e1d.png)

According to the rounded rectangle dimensions, the board is around 70x60 mm. Nice and compact. I'm also really happy with this new design; it's clean, cool, and leaves the perfect amount of space to add nice looking art. Hope it's just as nice to route, which is next on my agenda.

## Routing

I had a lot of trouble with the capacitors and resistors in the middle, because I was trying to wire all of its connections on F.cu. The reason why  is because whenever I switched from the front to back layer, all the thingy's colors would change from red to blue except those, so I figured maybe I had to keep those on the front? I wasn't sure, but better safe than sorry.

 It took quite a lot of shifting and undo-ing, but I was able to figure out a way to do it eventually. I also went ahead and routed all the rest of the +3V3 and GND connections on F.cu, as well as cleaned up all my lovely wires:
![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 12.53.09 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/45d98787ec5cf55be2a0d790f7d83992c4472c1a73a38b6316a59ef8743d5a05.png)

After that, I routed everything else on B.cu layer, which was luckily much more straightforward. I used vias whenever I had to connect to a capacitors or resistor.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 1.15.02 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/24033b6bb34fd747df3a20de05fe8142c7c0ecec094e96387e556f6931c681f3.png)

Next was the GND fill zone (which I had to google how to do) and then I ran the DRC which came back for no warnings, except these two:
![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 1.30.51 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/ce56ed69b2c77be3246f21b3c0e92c79ba29b07ccf3e64f2e424ccaf6c7d444f.png)

I ignored them because I remember doing the same thing in week 1 when i got those same errors. Hope it's not an issue.

Last but not least, added some silk screen art. Very important. Also the 3D model files (i had to download one for the display).

Final board :

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 3.54.58 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/a25f04e53b72e7d9aaaf926658fe3fbece9cc3e5ffaa88c97545eaec7d513f23.png)

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 3.55.30 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/dc0e1d455098e6b0cfc0d95715446f6abc4beb03aa61c874f261e8c326757350.png)

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 7.41.28 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UVNqyKra78p0fx3PyRp3K6pDIBVtreMb/015572aaca22759e2f0f46a8a0ce1ff52dcc6a3b41db9afa6cab06d134590628.png)

## Code
Now that there's one near-disastrous hurdle out of the way, it was time to actually code!

I am the the freshest of all beginners when it comes to coding, so for this part I had to ask for a lot guidance from my dad (and a little from AI).

What I wanted it to do was have one button start focus mode, another start short break, another start long break, and the last reset the timer. How our code does is first define what pins our buttons connect to in the ESP32-C3 and how long each timer duration is:

```
// Hardware Pin Definitions (GPIOs)
const int btnOne   = 2;   // KiCad Pin D0  -> Focus Mode
const int btnTwo   = 10;  // KiCad Pin D10 -> Short Break Mode
const int btnThree = 3;   // KiCad Pin D1  -> Long Break Mode
const int btnFour  = 20;  // KiCad Pin D7  -> Reset

// Timer Duration Targets (Converted to Seconds)
const unsigned long FOCUS_DURATION = 25 * 60;
const unsigned long SHORT_DURATION = 5 * 60;
const unsigned long LONG_DURATION  = 15 * 60;
```

It tracks the time by comparing the current time and last time and counting in milliseconds:

```
// State Machine Variables
enum TimerState { IDLE, FOCUS, SHORT_BREAK, LONG_BREAK };
TimerState currentState = IDLE;

unsigned long timeRemaining = 0; // Total seconds left in active cycle
unsigned long lastTickTime = 0;  // Tracks millisecond ticks for 1-second counting
```

This part assigns the buttons to their functions:
```
 // BUTTON ONE: Start / Continue Focus Mode
  if (digitalRead(btnOne) == LOW) {
    currentState = FOCUS;
    timeRemaining = FOCUS_DURATION;
    lastTickTime = millis();
    delay(250); // Debounce
  }
  // BUTTON TWO: Start Short Break
  else if (digitalRead(btnTwo) == LOW) {
    currentState = SHORT_BREAK;
    timeRemaining = SHORT_DURATION;
    lastTickTime = millis();
    delay(250); // Debounce
  }
  // BUTTON THREE: Start Long Break
  else if (digitalRead(btnThree) == LOW) {
    currentState = LONG_BREAK;
    timeRemaining = LONG_DURATION;
    lastTickTime = millis();
    delay(250); // Debounce
  }
  // BUTTON FOUR: System Reset
  else if (digitalRead(btnFour) == LOW) {
    currentState = IDLE;
    timeRemaining = 0;
    delay(250); // Debounce
```

And this deals with the transitions between different modes:

```
// Handle the automatic transition logic when a timer hits zero
      if (timeRemaining == 0) {
        if (currentState == FOCUS) {
          // Transition rule: Focus -> Short Break
          currentState = SHORT_BREAK;
          timeRemaining = SHORT_DURATION;
        }
        else if (currentState == SHORT_BREAK) {
          // Transition rule: Short Break -> Focus Mode
          currentState = FOCUS;
          timeRemaining = FOCUS_DURATION;
        }
        else if (currentState == LONG_BREAK) {
          // Transition rule: Long break stops entirely and returns to standard state
          currentState = IDLE;
        }
      }
```
There's still more to the code, of course, but I'm not going to explain each individual line.
